RoomType.rationale: HunterKillerNormal.cs:9 => RoomType.Monster. "hunter_killer" sits in `_hive_rooms().normal_keys` and nowhere else. No `Tags` override in the C# either, and correspondingly "hunter_killer" is absent from `_hive_rooms().tags` -- consistent.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: HunterKillerNormal.cs:11 declares a single-element list containing only `HunterKiller` -- exactly GenerateMonsters' one draw. Same consumer census as the rest of the batch: the property's only two real readers are UI/debug (dev-console unlock list, bestiary ratio), and the sim's real vocabulary need is satisfied by the global `_monster_classes()` walk regardless of any per-encounter declaration. Cost: none observed.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: HunterKillerNormal.cs:13-16: a single `HunterKiller` instance, `null` slot, zero RNG draws. `hunter_killer.py` does not override `create_monsters`; `HUNTER_KILLER_NORMAL = Encounter(id="hunter_killer_normal", monster_classes=[HunterKiller])` relies on the base class, which for one fixed class with no `monster_slots` produces `[HunterKiller(hooks, rng)]`, no slot assignment, zero draws off `selection_rng`. Roster, order, slot and draw count all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.cs:39` default (`=> false`), not overridden by the sealed `HunterKillerNormal`. The sim's `Encounter` is never a hook listener.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by HunterKillerNormal
guards.rationale: RoomType.Monster => 10-20 gold, matched by `rewards.py:170-173`'s `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]` (non-ascension baseline). `ShouldGiveRewards` default `true` matched by `Encounter.should_give_rewards`'s dataclass default, unmodified by `HUNTER_KILLER_NORMAL`.
